[[File:Wims-4.01e-accueil-fr.png|thumb|Screen shot of version 4.01 at the original University of Nice hosting.]]
The '''WWW Interactive Multipurpose Server (WIMS)''' (sometimes referred to as ''WWW Interactive Mathematics Server'') project is designed for supporting intensive [[mathematical exercise]]s via the [[Internet]] or in a computer-equipped classroom with server-side interactivity, accessible at the address http://wims.unice.fr.

The system has the following main features:
*A modular design allowing applications and software interfaces to be created and maintained independently from each other.
*Features interfaces for software including MuPAD, PARI/GP, [[Gnuplot]], [[POV-Ray]], Co.
*Dynamic rendering of mathematical formulas and animated graphics.
*A structure of virtual classes, including mechanisms for automatic score gathering and processing.
<ref>[http://wims.unice.fr/paper/wims/wims.html WIMS Paper]</ref>

The program is open source and freely available under the [[GNU General Public Licence]], however each WIMS module has its own copyright policy, which may differ from that of the server program.<ref name="copyr"/>

It is often cited and linked for its sophisticated "online calculator" tools capable of generating animated [[GIF]]s of parametric 2D or 3D graphs or allowing prime tests with very large numbers.

== Author ==
Xiao Gang was a professor at [[University of Nice Sophia Antipolis]]. He was interested in solar energy and algebraic geometry. He was also the active site manager of the WIMS of the university he worked for.<ref>[http://wims.unice.fr/xiao/xiao.html Homepage of Xiao Gang at wims.unice.fr]</ref> Xiao Gang died on June 27, 2014.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.mathadore.fr/xiao-gang-le-createur-de-wims-nous-a-quittes/ |title=Xiao Gang, le créateur de Wims nous a quittés (French) |access-date=2014-07-03 |archive-date=2014-11-29 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141129030731/http://www.mathadore.fr/xiao-gang-le-createur-de-wims-nous-a-quittes/ |url-status=dead }}</ref>

Xiao Gang taught himself during the [[Down to the Countryside Movement|Up to the Mountains and Down to the Countryside Movement]]. He obtained his master's degree from the [[University of Science and Technology of China]]. Xiao obtained his Ph.D. degree from [[University of Paris-Sud]] in 1984. Xiao Gang returned to China and became a lecturer at [[East China Normal University]]. He was promoted to professor in 1986, and was awarded the [[:zh:陈省身数学奖|Shiing-Shen Chern Prize in Mathematics]] in 1991. In 1992, Xiao became a professor at [[University of Nice Sophia Antipolis]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://wims.math.ecnu.edu.cn/wsysx/xiaog.html |title=Profile of Xiao Gang (Chinese) |access-date=2014-07-03 |archive-date=2021-04-14 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210414170113/http://wims.math.ecnu.edu.cn/wsysx/xiaog.html |url-status=dead }}</ref>
